lessons.name: every one of the 256 bytes keeps its low nibble under the version stamp
lessons.why: the version stamp on byte 6: (b & 0x0F) | 0x80 -/ def versionStamp (b : Nat) : Nat := or8 (and8 b 15) 128 /-- the variant stamp on byte 8: (b & 0x3F) | 0x80 -/ def variantStamp (b : Nat) : Nat := or8 (and8 b 63) 128 def bitAt (x i : Nat) : Nat := x / 2 ^ i % 2 /-- every byte 0 … 255, as sixteen high nibbles by sixteen low ones — exhaustive, and within the default recursion depth -/ def allBytes (p : Nat → Bool) : Bool := (List.range 16).all (fun hi => (List.range 16).all (fun lo => p (16 * hi + lo))) /-- the bit positions of a byte that a stamp sets to the same value for every input byte -/ def fixedPositions (stamp : Nat → Nat) : List Nat := (List.range 8).filter (fun i => allBytes (fun b => bitAt (stamp b) i == bitAt (stamp 0) i)) /-- every one of the 256 bytes keeps its low nibble under the version stamp
lessons.statement: allBytes (fun b => or8 (and8 b 15) 128 == 128 + b % 16) = true

lessons.name: for every map, value and bound, a search either finds the value or shows no input up to the bound has it
lessons.why: for every map, value and bound, a search either finds the value or shows no input up to the bound has it
lessons.statement: ∀ (f : Nat → Nat) (v n : Nat), (∃ x, x ≤ n ∧ f x = v) ∨ (∀ x, x ≤ n → f x ≠ v)

lessons.name: for every size n, any map of the n + 1 inputs into n values sends two of them to the same value
lessons.why: for every size n, any map of the n + 1 inputs into n values sends two of them to the same value
lessons.statement: ∀ (n : Nat) (f : Nat → Nat), (∀ x, x ≤ n → f x < n) → ∃ x y, x < y ∧ y ≤ n ∧ f x = f y

lessons.name: for every width k, any k-bit address of the 2^k + 1 inputs 0 … 2^k gives two of them the same address
lessons.why: for every width k, any k-bit address of the 2^k + 1 inputs 0 … 2^k gives two of them the same address
lessons.statement: ∀ (k : Nat) (f : Nat → Nat), (∀ x, f x < 2 ^ k) → ∃ x y, x < y ∧ y ≤ 2 ^ k ∧ f x = f y
